title: Authorization decisions toolkit and travel reimbursements
author: Sofia Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page compiles a single, practical toolkit for frontline decision-makers and people managers to handle access, change approvals, procurement thresholds, vendor onboarding, and travel reimbursement requests. The guidance below is normative: teams must follow the approval flows and use the included templates for auditability and consistency.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third parties who request or approve:
- IAM entitlements and application access
- Configuration and infra change window approvals
- Purchases, subscriptions, and one-off spend
- Vendor onboarding and renewals
- Business travel and related reimbursements

Owner and escalation: Finance-Legal owns the approval policy. Security owns technical access controls. People-ops owns traveler welfare and corporate card onboarding. Escalation path: approver -> team manager -> business unit lead -> Finance-Legal review. For security-sensitive access (data residency, production credentials) copy security@redwood.com on approval emails.

Table of contents:
1) Access & Permissions Decision Matrix
2) Change Management Approval Flow
3) Data Access & Usage Controls
4) Procurement & Expense Thresholds
5) Vendor Onboarding Checklist
6) Travel Policy and Reimbursements
7) Templates and Example Forms
8) Audit and Record Retention

1) Access & Permissions Decision Matrix

Principles:
- Least privilege by default; role-based groups preferred over individual grants.
- Time-boxed elevation for breakglass or emergency work; automatic expiry recommended.
- Separation of duties for production access: different approver required if requesting approver has admin rights.

Technical controls and services referenced:
- Identity Provider: Okta (primary SSO).
- Secrets and keys: HashiCorp Vault (application secrets) and AWS KMS (encryption keys).
- Cloud IAM: follow AWS/GCP account-level guardrails defined in infra-standards.

Decision matrix (summary):
- Routine developer access (non-prod cluster, CI logs): team manager approval.
- Production read-only (metrics, dashboards): team manager + SRE owner approval.
- Production write (deploys, DB write): engineering lead + SRE lead + security review.
- Cross-org access to PII or sensitive analytics: security + privacy + Finance-Legal approval.

Granting process (steps):
1. Request via Access Portal (link: https://okta.redwood.com/access-requests). Include justification, duration, and reviewer.
2. Manager reviews within 3 business days. Approvals auto-route to the next required role based on the matrix.
3. Provisioning action executed by automation (IAM roles or group assignment). If manual intervention required, the provisioning engineer records ticket ID.
4. Expiration: all non-permanent grants include an expiry date no greater than 90 days unless renewal is explicitly approved.

Emergency/Breach exceptions:
- Use the breakglass flow: page the oncall SRE and open an incident channel; emergency grants are time-limited to 4 hours and logged. Post-event review required within 5 business days.

2) Change Management Approval Flow

Change types and windows:
- Standard changes: low-risk config and deployments that follow an approved template; no additional approvals beyond normal CI/CD gates.
- Significant changes: schema migrations, infra capacity changes, or rollout of new model variants impacting production latency or cost. Require Engineering Product approval and SRE signoff.
- Emergency changes: P0 remediation with immediate action; follow the emergency exception above.

Approval SLA targets:
- Manager approval: 48 hours for standard/low risk.
- SRE review for significant changes: 5 business days for planned changes; can be expedited with justification.

Required artifacts for significant changes (submit in the change ticket):
- Owner, rollback procedure, blast radius estimate, monitoring and alert runbook, and load test summary.
- Risk table (example):
| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation | Owner |
|------|------------|------------|-------|
| Downtime of inference cluster | Medium | Canary rollout, auto-fallback | SRE |
| Latency regression > 2x | Low | Performance gate & abort on threshold | Runtime Team |

Rollout steps (numbered):
1. Create change ticket in ProcureFlow/ChangeBoard with required artifacts.
2. Run pre-deploy smoke tests in staging; attach logs.
3. Schedule canary hours and notify oncall with a runbook.
4. Monitor SLI dashboards for 30 minutes after canary; if no regressions, proceed staged rollout.
5. If rollback conditions hit, execute rollback and open retrospective.

3) Data Access & Usage Controls

Classification: All datasets must be classified at creation: public, internal, restricted, or regulated. Data owners are responsible for labeling.

Access controls by classification:
- Internal: default internal network access; manager-approved access.
- Restricted (contains PII or customer confidential): requires security review and access logging enabled; read-only where possible.
- Regulated (HIPAA/PCI-like): store in customer-managed private deployments; access controlled via Vault-issued short-lived credentials and audited every 30 days.

Retention and deletion: Follow the Data Retention Policy (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention). Retention windows must be documented at dataset creation. Data subject deletion requests are handled by Privacy + Legal.

4) Procurement & Expense Thresholds

Snapshot of approval thresholds (effective immediately):
- Up to $1,000: Requester + Manager approval; can use corporate card where issued.
- $1,001 to $25,000: Requester + Manager + Finance review; requires PO through ProcureFlow.
- $25,001 to $250,000: Requester + Manager + Finance + Procurement team review; legal review may be required for multi-year commitments.
- > $250,000: Executive sponsor + VP Finance sign-off + legal.

Corporate card and travel cards:
- Card issuance is managed by People-ops. New card requests require manager approval and training completion.
- Cardholders must attach itemized receipts within 7 days of transaction or the amount will be auto-determined and subject to manager review.

Reimbursement deadlines and receipts:
- Employees must submit receipts in Concur within 30 days of travel completion. Missing receipts above $75 require detailed justification and manager approval.

Competitive bidding and vendor selection:
- For purchases > $25,000, at least two competitive bids are required unless documented sole-source justification exists.
- RFP process handled by Procurement team; templates available in the Templates section below.

5) Vendor Onboarding Checklist

Minimum required items before a vendor is approved for production use:
- Commercial contract signed by Legal; term sheet saved in ContractVault (link).
- Security questionnaire completed and reviewed by security team.
- Required insurance certificates on file (certificate of insurance with cyber liability minimum $1M).
- Data processing agreement (if vendor handles customer data).
- Technical onboarding checklist: IP allowlist, SSO integration (Okta SAML or SCIM), minimum TLS 1.2, and logging endpoints configured.

Renewals and audit cadence:
- Annual security re-review for high-risk vendors.
- Contract renewals > $100k escalate to Procurement + Legal for negotiation strategy.

6) Travel Policy and Reimbursements

Pre-approval and booking:
- All business travel must be pre-approved by manager. For international travel, allow 10 business days for approvals.
- Preferred booking channels: Concur for flights and hotels; company-negotiated partners are required for bookings where available.

Per diem and allowable costs:
- Lodging: use negotiated hotel rates where available; exceptions allowed with manager approval.
- Meals: per diem cap $75/day (USD) for domestic travel; $100/day for international travel unless higher country allowance is approved. Receipts required for all meal claims.
- Ground transport: Use taxis or company-approved rideshare; mileage reimbursed at IRS standard rate for personal vehicle use.

Errata and special cases:
- Upgrades (business class) require Executive sponsor approval for flights >8 hours or where medical need is documented.
- Visa and immunization costs are reimbursable when pre-approved by People-ops.

Reimbursement process (numbered):
1. Submit travel expense report in Concur within 30 days with all receipts attached.
2. Manager reviews and certifies expenses within 7 days.
3. Finance processes reimbursement on the next payroll cycle; urgent reimbursements may be requested through People-ops.

Example expense table (for approver quick reference):
| Item | Documentation required | Approval level | Notes |
|------|-----------------------|----------------|-------|
| Hotel | Itemized receipt | Manager | Use negotiated rates where possible |
| Meal > $75 | Itemized receipt + justification | Manager | International per diem exceptions possible |
| Flight upgrade | Approval email | Executive sponsor | Only for >8 hour flights or medical needs |

7) Templates and Example Forms

Included templates (store in the Templates library and reference in tickets):
- Access request template: access-request-template.docx (fields: requester, justification, duration, approver)
- Change ticket template: change-ticket-template.md (fields: owner, rollback, impact, test plan)
- Procurement RFP template: rfp-template.xlsx
- Vendor security questionnaire: security-questionnaire.pdf
- Travel pre-approval form: travel-preapproval-form.pdf
- Expense report checklist: expense-checklist.md

When to use which template: Always attach the matching template for the change/procurement type. Missing artifacts will delay approvals.

8) Audit, Evidence and Record Retention

Record retention rules:
- Access approvals, change tickets, and procurement POs are archived for a minimum of 7 years in the ContractVault and AuditStore.
- Sensitive vendor security docs (questionnaires) are retained for the contract duration + 3 years.

Audit readiness and evidence collection:
- For access reviews, teams must run quarterly entitlement reports from Okta and reconcile with recorded approvals. Failure to reconcile triggers an audit remediation plan.
- For vendor audits, Procurement will collect SOC2 or equivalent evidence and coordinate with Security for any remediation items.

Appendix: Quick decision flow examples

Scenario A — Developer needs temporary production DB write access for a hotfix:
1. Developer creates Access Request with justification and 4-hour duration.
2. Manager approves; SRE lead receives auto-route and approves due to emergency.
3. Provisioning engineer applies role and records change ticket ID.
4. Immediately after, an incident review is scheduled to document blast radius and post-change validation.

Scenario B — Purchasing a new SaaS observability tool for $45,000/yr:
1. Requester completes RFP template and obtains two bids.
2. Manager approves; Procurement and Finance review pricing and contract terms.
3. Legal reviews the vendor contract; insurance and security questionnaires are completed.
4. Finance issues PO and records are archived in ContractVault.

Contacts and escalation list:
- Finance-Legal: finance-legal@redwood.com
- Security intake: security@redwood.com
- Procurement team: procurement@redwood.com
- People-ops travel: people-ops@redwood.com
